verdict.rationale: Fedora's own docs say the desktop is free with no ads and that your data is yours, which speaks to freedom from vendor lock-in. Hands-on reports show successful installs on varied laptops (Framework AMD, a budget Lenovo, VAIO), but the evidence also shows Nvidia driver trouble, freezes on low-end hardware, and VirtualBox display glitches. There is also no first-party hardware-compatibility documentation. Missing for 10: first-party documentation of supported hardware/architectures, smooth proprietary GPU (Nvidia) driver support, reliable behavior on low-end hardware and in third-party hypervisors.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can install and use the OS without vendor lock-in on hardware of my choosing

citations.quote: With Fedora, your desktop is your own. It's free, there are no ads, and your data belongs to you.
Running Fedora 39 on a new Framework AMD Ryzen laptop: relatively minimal hiccups getting it going, and it seems great now.
Replaced Windows on a $480 Lenovo laptop with Fedora 39, and it became a full Python development workstation quickly.
